name: Kiss of the Dragon
summary: Kiss of the Dragon is a reverse De La Riva inversion that takes the bottom player underneath the opponent's near leg to reach the backside and pursue rear control.
description: Kiss of the Dragon is a reverse De La Riva inversion that takes the bottom player underneath the opponent's near leg to reach the backside and pursue rear control.
overview:
The bottom player has a reverse De La Riva hook against a standing or crouching passer, with space for shoulder-supported inversion. It begins from guard below the opponent, not from a top turtle ride. Reaching behind the legs is a checkpoint; complete back control still requires torso attachment and leg control.

Use the reverse hook and lower-leg connection while facing the standing passer. Load weight onto the far leg or available post to create space beside the near leg. Turn onto the shoulder and upper back, keeping weight off the neck.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Giancarlo Bodoni — reverse De La Riva inversion](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkT6Mpn5uLY); [Rob Biernacki and Stephan Kesting — no-gi De La Riva](https://www.grapplearts.com/no-gi-de-la-riva/).

attacker.name: Kiss of the Dragon Attacker
attacker.description: Kiss of the Dragon (attacker): Use the reverse hook and lower-leg connection while facing the standing passer. Load weight onto the far leg or available post to create space beside the near leg.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player has a reverse De La Riva hook against a standing or crouching passer, with space for shoulder-supported inversion. It begins from guard below the opponent, not from a top turtle ride. Reaching behind the legs is a checkpoint; complete back control still requires torso attachment and leg control.

Use the reverse hook and lower-leg connection while facing the standing passer. Load weight onto the far leg or available post to create space beside the near leg. Turn onto the shoulder and upper back, keeping weight off the neck.

Bring the head and tucked knee through the space with a controlled pendulum action. Connect behind the thigh while bringing the knees behind the opponent's leg line. Establish torso and leg control before calling the result back control; return to guard if the connection is lost.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Keep the inside elbow close to the knee as the reverse De La Riva hook and grips create the opening for inversion. The foot on the hip supplies hip control for a compact pivot while the knee follows the head under the near leg. Preserve guard retention if the backside opening closes; release an unsafe leg capture and rebuild facing frames rather than forcing the roll.

flashcards.question: Kiss of the Dragon (bottom): What remains after you reach behind the legs?
flashcards.answer: Establish torso and leg control before calling the result back control; return to guard if the connection is lost.

plausible: Ankle grip alone, chest beside hip
Rear torso grip, legs disengaged
trap: Leg hook, chest still facing them

flashcards.question: Kiss of the Dragon (bottom): Why move weight away from the near leg before entering underneath?
flashcards.answer: Use the reverse hook and off-balance to move weight toward the far leg or available post. The near-leg opening then admits the head and tucked knee on a shoulder-supported turn.
flashcards.answer_line: Room for head and tucked knee

plausible: Near knee stays heavy as head passes
No need to bring your knee beneath
trap: Head enters, tucked knee stays out

flashcards.question: Kiss of the Dragon (bottom): What makes a huge straight-leg pendulum a poor choice here?
flashcards.answer: Bodoni favors drawing the knee inward over a large straight-leg swing that the opponent can capture.
flashcards.answer_line: Exposes leg, loses compact knee path

plausible: Long leg keeps hooked knee compact
Pendulum replaces the off-balance

flashcards.question: Kiss of the Dragon (bottom): The opening closes around your head or leg. What should you do?
flashcards.answer: If the shoulder-supported path closes, return to frames and guard retention instead of forcing a trapped neck or leg.

plausible: Turn hips with head still wedged
Reach hamstring, lower leg fixed
trap: Switch swing leg, head still stuck

flashcards.question: Kiss of the Dragon (bottom): What role does the foot on the hip play in the compact turn?
flashcards.answer: The foot-on-hip connection supports the pivot as the knee tucks and the head passes under the near leg.
flashcards.answer_line: A pivot as knee draws to chest

plausible: A push with knee extended outside
A pivot without hand-leg contact
trap: Fixed hips, only head goes under

defender.overview:

A bottom player turning under the near leg from reverse De La Riva is seeking backside access. Redistribute weight before the far leg and posting arm are loaded. Clear the reverse hook before the opponent has inverted under the knee line.

Turn with the opponent while keeping the knee aligned rather than spinning on a trapped foot. Face the guard player again before their torso and legs secure the back. Never drive the inverted partner onto the neck to stop the movement.
